question: Can a class-balanced, CV-tuned model match or beat a standard MLP perception stand-in on macro-F1 while giving lower per-sample inference latency and better accuracy under input noise?
method: Stratified 75/25 split of scikit-learn digits; features standardised on training data. Baseline MLPClassifier (128 hidden units) vs class-balanced RBF SVM with C and gamma chosen by 3-fold stratified CV (macro-F1) on training data. Test metrics, latency and noisy accuracy computed for both; repeated for seeds 42, 43, 44.
baseline: scikit-learn MLPClassifier, one hidden layer of 128 units, trained on standardised pixels
improved: Class-balanced RBF-kernel SVM (SVC); C and gamma selected by 3-fold stratified CV on the training split only
notes: Digits is a small stand-in for camera perception, not a driving dataset, so results do not show real-world performance. The improved model was changed from LightGBM to an RBF SVM after LightGBM trailed the baseline on macro-F1; the baseline and test split are unchanged. Noise is Gaussian sigma=2.0 on the raw pixel scale, one fixed draw shared by both models. Latency is mean wall-clock time per single-sample predict() over 200 test rows on this runner; it is hardware-dependent. Std values are across seeds [42, 43, 44]; the test split is identical for all. Chosen SVM params per seed: [{'C': 100, 'gamma': 0.01}, {'C': 1, 'gamma': 0.02}, {'C': 10, 'gamma': 0.01}].
